justification.dataset: 000986 is a canonical pure-tone auditory-cortex set, but per the rubric pure tones cannot demonstrate a true spectrotemporal receptive field, so only a frequency-response-area over time can be shown.
justification.handling: Data are correctly streamed from DANDI and trial-aligned by frequency and onset, but no spike-sorting quality criteria are applied beyond the functional responsiveness test.
justification.analysis: Reverse-correlation PSTH stacking is appropriate for this sparse-tone design, but best frequency is selected by argmax and then significance is tested at that same frequency without correcting for the best-of-5 selection.
justification.correctness: The 891/1564 (57%) headline reproduces from the committed code and is internally consistent with the figures; numbers are physically plausible, with only the mild selection-bias caveat.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, show restricted frequency bands and short-latency responses, and example units are chosen by response strength rather than a flattering unrelated criterion.
justification.honesty: The strong result is not misrepresented and examples are representative, but calling the pure-tone map 'exactly the STRF' overstates it and no limitation about stimulus richness or the best-of-5 test is stated.
justification.verdict: Sound, reproducible, well-presented work whose core deliverable is really a frequency-tuning-over-time map rather than a true STRF, so I would accept it after asking for the pure-tone limitation and multiple-comparison caveat to be added.
